findings.area: symbol_door wall band limit (openings.py:1852-1853, hunk 'wall band must be thinner than 0.6 - EPS')
findings.summary: OB.section(..., n, 0.6) clips the band of any wall thicker than 0.6 m to exactly 0.6 m. BEFORE's `b - a <= 0.6` accepted that clipped band; AFTER's `b - a < 0.6 - EPS` rejects it, so every door symbol on a wall of 0.6 m or more (drawn through or cut at the door) loses the wall: thickness becomes 0.1, the door centre moves onto the wall face (0.3 m off the centre line of a 0.6 m wall, 0.4 m for 0.8 m, 0.5 m for 1.0 m) and, for a wall drawn through, host becomes 'none'. The four twins of the same limit stay inclusive (openings.py:843, 992, 1173, 1230 use `<= 0.6`), so one rule treats a 0.6 m wall as a wall and symbol_door does not. Only L30-034 gains (key x 2.471: BEFORE 2.2213, AFTER 2.5213) and the six drawings have no wall over 0.5 m, so the harness cannot see the loss.
findings.expected: A door symbol on a 0.6-1.0 m wall keeps the wall (BEFORE: thickness 0.6, host wall).
findings.actual: Wall drawn through, door symbol on its face, 20 placements: 0.60 m wall AFTER door t=0.10, centre y +0.30, host none in 19/20 (BEFORE t=0.60 centred, host wall 20/20); 0.80 m: host none 18/20 (BEFORE wall); 1.00 m: host none 20/20. Wall cut at the door: 0.60 m BEFORE t 0.60 centred, AFTER t 0.10 centre +0.30; 0.80 m AFTER t 0.10 centre +0.40 and the end moves to x 3.05 (opening ends at 3.0).
findings.repro: cd CODE/synth && PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python -B t03_symbol_door_06.py ; PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python -B t03b_thick_wall_cut.py   (CODE = ...fix4/review_final/code)
findings.suggestedFix: Use `b - a <= 0.6 + EPS` like the other four 0.6 m wall limits (clipped bands of thick walls then stay accepted), and settle L30-034 another way (for example reject a band that is a merge of two wall pieces), or widen the section window so a thick wall is measured instead of clipped.

findings.area: geomkit.Prim.poly keeps only the largest polygon (geomkit.py:168-170) and small_shapes (openings.py:610)
findings.summary: For a closed outline whose buffer(0) is a MultiPolygon (two lobes wound the same way: a ring that touches itself, two wall pieces drawn in ONE polyline over a zero-width bridge) BEFORE kept every lobe in the wall solid; AFTER keeps only the larger, so the other wall piece, and the gap beside it, silently vanish. The hunk is redundant: the crash it targets (jamb_at reading .exterior of a small MultiPolygon, presidential with 5 mm vertex jitter, seeds 1 and 2 crash BEFORE) is already fixed by small_shapes iterating polys(). With the geomkit hunk reverted and small_shapes kept, 12 jitter runs have 0 crashes and the scene below gives BEFORE's result. After the hunk Prim.poly is always one Polygon, so `polys(p.poly)` in small_shapes is a no-op and its comment ('a self-crossing outline buffers to several polygons') is stale. On the six real drawings 20 such outlines exist (Sukhumvit 19, L29 1) and none is on a wall or column layer, so the harness is unchanged.
findings.expected: Both wall pieces stay in the wall solid (as BEFORE and ORIGINAL).
findings.actual: Wall A x 0..6 and wall B x 7.5..11 (0.2 thick) in one closed polyline, B wound the other way: BEFORE wall parts [(0,-0.1,6,0.1),(7.5,-0.1,11,0.1)] and a 1.5 m passage; AFTER wall parts [(0,-0.1,6,0.1)] and nothing.
findings.repro: cd CODE/synth && PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python -B t01b_multipolygon_wall.py ; count on real data: python -B CODE/scripts/count_multipoly.py ; crash check: python -B CODE/scripts/jit_crash.py <dir> 0.005 1,2 with dir = CODE/before (2 crashes), CODE/after, CODE/after_nogk (0 crashes each)
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the geomkit change (keep self.poly = g, MultiPolygon allowed) and rely on small_shapes' polys(); or split a MultiPolygon outline into one Prim per polygon so no piece is lost.

findings.area: find_strips thickness limit `t < tmax - EPS` (openings.py:272) with the thin-screen call (openings.py:1309: find_strips(fl.W, 0.005, 0.03, 0.3)) and the wall call (tmin 0.03, no EPS)
findings.summary: The EPS was applied to the upper limit only, and exclusive, which opens a dead zone 0.0295 <= t < 0.03 that neither the thin-screen call nor the wall call accepts. A glass screen drawn 29.5-30 mm (rule 6 says '5-30 mm') is no strip at all. BEFORE found every such strip as a screen or as a wall strip. The EPS comment (openings.py:125-126) says comparisons are inclusive; this one and F1 are exclusive.
findings.expected: Every thickness is a wall strip or a thin screen.
findings.actual: Rectangles 3 m x t at 400 random sheet positions: t = 0.0299: BEFORE found as thin screen 400/400, AFTER 0/400 (found by neither 400); t = 0.0300 exactly: found by neither 0/400 BEFORE, 81/400 AFTER. (t = 0.5500 and 0.5499 are no strip in AFTER, as intended.)
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the tolerance on both sides of the 0.03 hand-over (wall call tmin 0.03 - EPS, screen call tmax 0.03 + EPS minus nothing), or leave the screen call inclusive; at least keep the two calls complementary.
